title: Load the rate card when it is needed, and again after a failure

blocks.text: The pricing service converts every price with a rate card that it loads from the rate service. Two incidents last quarter:

items: The rate service was down for ten minutes. The pricing service's health check, which calls `RateCard.version()`, failed too, so the orchestrator restarted the pricing pods over and over.
At one startup the rate service timed out once. It answered again a second later, but every price request failed until the pods were restarted by hand.

blocks.text: At startup a few hundred requests arrive together, and the rate service allows one load per pod.

Finish the `TODO` in `rates()` in `src/main/java/practice/RateCard.java`. When you're done, the health check answers whatever the rate service is doing, a request whose load fails gets the rate service's own error and the next request tries again, and requests that arrive together while the rates are loading wait for that one load. About six lines in total.
Each test loads a fresh copy of `RateCard` through a class loader of its own, so every test starts as if the pod had just started.

cases.says: prices use the rates the rate service returned, and repeated requests reuse one load
the health check answers while the rate service is down, and prices work once it is back
a request whose load fails gets the rate service's own error, and the next request loads the rates and succeeds
two requests that arrive while the first load is still running ask the rate service once between them

origin.section: A Static Initializer That Throws Leaves the Class Unusable Until the JVM Restarts

concepts: A static initializer that throws is never run again: the first use gets ExceptionInInitializerError and every later use NoClassDefFoundError until the JVM restarts.
Work that can fail belongs in a method that can be called again, not in a static initializer; a holder class makes the load lazy but not retryable.
